reference_sql:
SELECT brand, COUNT(*) AS n_bad
FROM products
WHERE sku <> UPPER(REPLACE(sku, ' ', ''))
GROUP BY brand
alternatives:
SELECT brand, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE sku <> UPPER(REPLACE(sku, ' ', ''))) AS n_bad
FROM products
GROUP BY brand
HAVING COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE sku <> UPPER(REPLACE(sku, ' ', ''))) > 0
SELECT brand, COUNT(*) AS n_bad FROM products WHERE sku <> REPLACE(UPPER(sku), ' ', '') GROUP BY brand

other_way.sql:
SELECT brand, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE sku <> UPPER(REPLACE(sku, ' ', ''))) AS n_bad
FROM products
GROUP BY brand
HAVING COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE sku <> UPPER(REPLACE(sku, ' ', ''))) > 0
other_way.tradeoff: Counting with FILTER and keeping brands with HAVING works on all products at once, but filtering rows in WHERE is simpler.
